summary: Stevens County, WA tower built 1923-1927 near Orient; replaced 1938, moved to Quartz Mountain 1955, burned there 1997; no source describes the original site today.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with 7'x7' cab (1927); replaced in 1938 by a 53-foot timber tower with L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Tower moved to Quartz Mountain in 1955 and destroyed by arson there in 1997; no source describes the original site today

events.note: Site established as a camp, per firelookout.com
First tower built June 1923 (WillhiteWeb); a September 1923 item says completed by the first of July
7-by-7-foot cab added to the 40-foot pole tower (WillhiteWeb); register and firelookout.com date the 40-foot pole tower with this cab to 1927
Morris Ewell named as lookout (WillhiteWeb); a 1928 newspaper item calls him a nephew stationed at the lookout; firelookout.com dates him to 1929
Clarence Rhode named as lookout; a 1934 newspaper item refers to the previous season
53-foot timber tower with L-4 cab replaced the 40-foot pole tower
Patricia Langdon named as lookout in 1945
Tower moved to Quartz Mountain, near Republic
At Quartz Mountain: L-4 cab removed, tower trimmed to 30 feet, R-6 flat cab added
At Quartz Mountain: arson destroyed the tower in October 1997
Registered November 23, 2012 as FFLOS US 1489; nominated by Ray Kresek

notes_for_editor: Conflicts: first tower year 1922 camp / 1923 tower (WillhiteWeb, 1923 newspaper) / 1927 pole tower (register, firelookout.com); the story gives 1923 for the first tower and notes the 1927 cab. Morris Ewell: 1928 (WillhiteWeb, 1928 newspaper) vs 1929 (firelookout.com). The Quartz tower is the moved Churchill tower; it was burned in October 1997, so no structure stands at either site. The Churchill site has no described current condition beyond a 'Churchill Footings' photo caption on WillhiteWeb. No access information found for the Churchill site, so no access key was written. The NGS designation 'Churchill Lookout Tower' is a survey mark name only. Record status 'gone' and elevation 1465 m match the register. Quartz Mountain site is itself gone (not a new lookout record). No new photos with usable URLs and licences were found.
